Title: Collector Sidecar Proxy Pattern and Evidence Telemetry Spec

Purpose
This doc defines a lightweight collector-sidecar + proxy pattern for evidence automation at Redwood Inference. Goal: provide a resilient, low-latency path to capture control evidence (RBAC v2 events, config changes, model rollouts, private deployment activity) and reliably deliver structured audit records to the evidence lake and SIEM export streams with minimal impact to product paths.

Scope
- Collector responsibilities: capture event payloads, enrich with provenance metadata, sign envelopes for proof-of-origin, buffer on disk when downstream is unavailable.
- Proxy responsibilities: provide an authenticated local HTTP/gRPC ingestion endpoint for product services and forward normalized events to the centralized evidence router (Kafka topics and S3-compatible staging).
- Out of scope: long-term archival policies (handled by evidence-retention), analytics pipelines downstream.

Motivation and constraints
- Many services cannot block on remote systems. We need a local-sidecar that accepts events synchronously, acknowledges quickly, and handles retries asynchronously.
- Reduce coupling between teams by standardizing a minimal client contract (HTTP POST /v1/evidence) and letting the sidecar handle batching, compression, signing, and export mapping.
- Ensure cryptographic proofs for chain-of-custody and defensible evidence for audits: each envelope includes signer key id, signature algorithm, and optional HSM-backed signing for Dedicated/Private deployments.

High-level architecture
1) Service emits a lightweight event to local sidecar (HTTP/gRPC). Fast path: ack within <10ms.
2) Sidecar performs schema validation and enrichment (service name, instance id, container id, region, RBAC v2 actor metadata if present).
3) Sidecar signs envelope (optional based on policy), persists to local journal, and enqueues for export.
4) Exporter component in sidecar groups events into batches by destination (evidence-stream, siem-export) and applies transformation/mapping.
5) Batches are forwarded to central router over TLS mTLS (mutual auth). On network failure, sidecar enters exponential backoff and continues local journaling until retries succeed.

Collector sidecar behavior
- Minimal dependencies: static binary or small container image (<60MB compressed) with single config file.
- Run modes: daemonset (k8s), sidecar per pod, or systemd on VM. Mode selected by deployment manifest.
- APIs:
  - POST /v1/evidence (application/json-lines) -> returns {"status":"accepted","receipt_id":"<uuid>"}
  - GET /v1/health -> liveness and backpressure signals
  - POST /v1/flush (admin) -> force immediate export
- Local persistence: append-only journal in /var/lib/redwood-evidence/journal; rotate daily and keep N segments configurable.
- Backpressure: when local disk > 85% use, respond 429 with Retry-After header and emit telemetry event to local tracer.

Event schema (normalized audit envelope)
- top-level fields (flat):
  - envelope_id (uuid)
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - event_type (rbac.v2.change | audit.api.call | model.rollout | config.change | deploy.action)
  - origin_service (string)
  - environment (prod|staging|dev)
  - actor_id (string) // from RBAC v2 system if available
  - actor_type (user|service|support)
  - resource_type (route|model|cluster|secret)
  - resource_id (string)
  - change_summary (short text)
  - delta (optional JSON string - small) // avoid large blobs in first-class events
  - evidence_level (0|1|2) // 0=soft, 2=control-critical
  - provenance: keys (signer_id, signature, algorithm) OR provenance_url (if HSM external)
  - routing_hint (siem:audit, evidence:high-integrity, metrics:telemetry)

Mapping to SIEM export
- SIEM expects line-delimited JSON with these mapping rules:
  - siem_event_id -> envelope_id
  - siem_timestamp -> timestamp
  - siem_actor -> actor_id + actor_type
  - siem_action -> event_type
  - siem_resource -> resource_type:resource_id
  - siem_context -> concatenation of origin_service + environment + change_summary
- Sidecar enforces an optional PII scrubber on siem export path (configurable regex allowlist) in order to avoid sending secrets or raw user content.

Control evidence workflows (example)
1) RBAC v2 policy change: web UI triggers PUT to auth-api. auth-api posts event to local sidecar with event_type=rback.v2.change. Sidecar signs and exports to evidence-stream with evidence_level=2 and routing_hint=evidence:high-integrity.
2) Dedicated deployment key rotation: infra service posts to /v1/evidence with resource_type=secret and evidence_level=2. Sidecar persists locally and attempts immediate mTLS push to HSM-backed attest gateway for signature.
3) Canary model rollback: serving-runtime emits model.rollout with delta compressed link to artifact in S3; sidecar includes artifact pointer rather than embedding binary.

Resilience and verification
- Every envelope includes envelope_id and signer metadata; central evidence router verifies signatures on ingest and records verification result as a meta-attribute.
- Replay-friendliness: sidecar journal segments are strictly ordered. Router can request a segment-range if rehydration is needed.
- Idempotency: receipts include content-hash; central router deduplicates by content-hash + envelope_id.

Retention and TTL
- Sidecar journal: short-lived (configure default 7 days). Central evidence lake retention policies controlled by compliance team.
- SIEM export: high-volume low-ttl (90 days) for detailed events, with extracted indicators forwarded to long-term store.

Operational concerns
- Observability: traces for each accepted event (sampling configurable), metrics for queue depth, failed batches, disk pressure, signature failures.
- Alerts:
  - queue_depth > threshold for 10m
  - signature_failures > 1% over 1h
  - backpressure responses exceed 5% of requests
- Upgrades: sidecar supports rolling upgrade via graceful shutdown; journal is migrated automatically.

Privacy and security notes
- Default behavior: scrub values matching credit_card and ssn regex patterns before export.
- Admins can enable stronger scrubbing for hosted customers; Private deployment config allows customers to opt for HSM-only signing and disable external routing.

Operational runbook (summary)
- Normal failure: restart sidecar, check journal integrity (journal-check tool), resume export.
- Network partition: sidecar remains writeable; monitor disk and trigger emergency archival to NFS if disk exceeds 95%.
- Evidence corruption: router-level verification fails -> quarantine topic + alert to security oncall + fallback to raw-staging bucket with mtime and verifier notes.

Development and rollout plan
- Phase 1 (Q1): implement basic sidecar with local journal, signing stub, and Kafka export. Minimal config. Testing in staging with sample product services.
- Phase 2 (Q2): HSM integration, SIEM export mapping, PII-scrubber, and per-tenant policies.
- Phase 3 (Q3): Dedicated/private deployment feature gates (HSM-only signing, local-only export), hardening, and compliance audit run.

Open questions / decisions
- Should we standardize a canonical set of event_type values across products, or allow teams to extend with namespace prefixes?
- Signing key rotation cadence and key provenance model for Hosted vs Private customers.
- Central policy for PII scrubbing: default conservative vs per-team opt-outs.

References and links
- See linked artifacts for related Jira tickets, PRs, and Confluence notes. Slack thread: #sec-evidence (pinned: discussion 2024-10-11). 

Author notes
- This is intended as a working spec. Implementation details will iterate based on compatibility testing with serving-runtime and infra teams. Expectations: low-latency ack, durability under partition, and cryptographic provenance for audit-grade evidence.
